text:
sanjay: heads up — noticed a p99 latency burst in the canary pool after runtime v2.7.1 rolled ~10m ago. Affects auth-heavy tenants, p95 looks fine. dashboard: https://dash/reports/rt/p99 :eyes:

maria: can you paste a sample request + headers? also which cohort/tenant id is showing the spike?

sanjay: sample path: POST /v1/generate
headers: Authorization: Bearer <token-redacted>
payload: {
  "model": "redwood-turbo-13b",
  "input": "Summarize this..."
}
tenant: acme-cohort-a

deploy-bot: rollout v2.7.1 -> canary completed (workers=45) at 2024-11-12T14:22:37Z :white_check_mark:

alex: grabbing traces now. Initial look: many spans stuck waiting on auth/permfetch and then long gpu-queue wait. Also seeing elevated connection resets from auth service.

chen: did we flip the kernel-selector or scheduler change in this rollout? there was a commit that touched quant/kernel fallback last week (fa1b2c).

sanjay: yes fa1b2c landed in the canary image. It toggles the kernel-selector heuristic and bumps tenant-scheduler limits.

maria: quick repro idea: route 5% of acme-cohort-a traffic to prev runtime and compare p99. if it drops -> regression in runtime. can someone run that split?

alex: I ran a 2-min split: directing 10% away to v2.7.0 dropped p99 from 820ms -> 170ms for the same request trace. p95 unchanged.

maria: that strongly suggests the new runtime path. do we have kernel-level traces? please capture the top blocked syscall stacks + gpu queue depth for a few slow requests.

alex: pasted a short trace sample:
```
span: request/12345
  wait auth (permfetch) 320ms
  kernel queue wait 410ms
  model execute 60ms
  total 820ms
logs: auth service returned 200 but with latency spike and intermittent 502 from permfetch cache
```

chen: two hypotheses: 1) kernel-selector picks a slower quant path for these shapes under new heuristic, causing kernel queue backpressure; 2) auth permfetch has a slow-path (cold kvcache) that exacerbates tail when combined with scheduler pacing. either could amplify p99 while leaving p95 intact.

sanjay: agree. immediate mitigations: (A) revert kernel-selector flag in canary (quick toggle), (B) throttle cohort A away from canary to limit customer impact, (C) increase sampling and enable full traces for auth-permfetch calls.

maria: add path-level sampling for /v1/generate to 100% for acme-cohort-a for 15m. also expand stored spans to include gpu-queue depth.

deploy-bot: rollback flag toggle available: `runtime.kernel_selector=false` (will take ~45s to propagate).

alex: toggled kernel_selector=false on canary nodes at 14:42:10Z. re-checking metrics... p99 dropped to ~190ms within 2 minutes. still monitoring. :thumbsup:

sanjay: great — that looks like the kernel selector change is causal. next: run a bisect between fa1b2b (pre) and fa1b2c (post) to find the exact heuristic line. open a PR to split the heuristic into a safer rollout.

maria: opened INC-2324 for customer-impact and escalated to SRE. incident notes: impacted tenants: acme-cohort-a (partial), peak p99 820ms, mitigated by kernel_selector toggle, action: full bisect + safer flag-driven rollout.

inc-bot: incident INC-2324 created by maria at 2024-11-12T14:50:02Z.

chen: for the bisect plan: run unit of change tests that toggle only the kernel heuristic, then smoke-test with auth-heavy sampled requests. we should also add a perf regression test into CI that simulates permfetch cold kvcache.

alex: logging notes for postmortem: attach perf flame for the 820ms sample, trace id 12345, and the deployment manifest with image sha. also note that the scheduler limit bump amplified queueing when kernel path slowed.

sanjay: final checklist for now: 1) keep kernel_selector=false in canary for 24h, 2) run bisect + create minimal revert PR for the heuristic line, 3) add CI perf test for auth-heavy path, 4) coordinate postmortem and customer comms.

maria: assigning follow-ups: @chen bisect + PR, @alex gather traces + flame, @sanjay coordinate customer comms and rollback window.

sanjay: I'll draft a short note to affected teams and the CSMs. thanks everyone — we'll update the thread when bisect has a clear culprit.
